ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Two objects A and B start from rest at the same time from the same position and move in a straight line in the same direction. Their displacement-time (x-t) graph of motion is shown in the figure. At what time are the two objects A and B farthest apart?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The two objects A and B are farthest apart at time t=t_{0}.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the graph: The figure is a displacement-time graph, with the vertical axis labeled as displacement x and the horizontal axis labeled as time t. On the horizontal axis there are graduations such as t0, 2t0, 3t0, 4t0, 5t0, and 6t0, and on the vertical axis there are x0 and 2x0. Both curves A and B start from the origin O. Curve A first rises rapidly, reaches the highest position of about 2x0 at t0, and then slopes downward; curve B rises more slowly from the origin, reaches about x0 near the later time of about 5t0, and then descends. In the figure, at t=t0, A is obviously at a high position, while B is still at a relatively low displacement, and the vertical distance between the two curves is the greatest; afterward A descends and B rises, and the vertical distance between them gradually decreases. In the later stage, even if B is above A, the distance is also smaller than that at t0. Then reason: At the same moment, the two objects move along the same straight line in the same direction, and their distance is equal to the absolute value of the difference between the two displacements at that moment, that is, the vertical distance between the two curves on the x-t graph. Comparing the vertical distance between curves A and B in the figure at each time, the maximum vertical distance occurs at time t=t0. Therefore, the two objects A and B are farthest apart at t=t0.
